findings.problem: The residual audit accepts absolute paths with repeated leading separators. Its POSIX branch excludes //, while its UNC branch requires exactly two leading separators and a later share separator. Thus ///home/synthetic-review-user/private.txt and //synthetic-private survive unchanged into a successful opt-in archive. This contradicts the promised refusal of unsafe residuals.
findings.reproduction: In the pinned test Fixture, retained_result(notes='///home/synthetic-review-user/private.txt'); archived(redact_repository_paths=True) succeeds and the archived research-review-0001.json retains that exact synthetic absolute path. Repeating with //synthetic-private also succeeds.
findings.windows_assessment: Direct public_files probes refuse canonical C:\synthetic-private\probe.txt, C:/synthetic-private/probe.txt, and standard UNC paths. A three-leading-backslash host/share path is accepted despite ntpath.isabs returning true. Single-leading-backslash paths are not treated as fully absolute by the available ntpath implementation and are not a separate finding.
findings.required_result: Refuse repeated-leading-separator absolute forms outside the documented URL/template exceptions, with regression cases for POSIX and Windows forms; refuse the entire archive before writing. Preserve HTTP(S) citations and legitimate relative paths.
